title: The GOP is Defunding the Tax Policy, Making America Great for Rich Tax Cheats
author: Algernon Austin
content:
> Donald J. Trump paid $750 in federal income taxes the year he won the
> presidency [in 2016]. In his first year in the White House, he paid another
> $750. He had paid no income taxes at all in 10 of the previous 15 years —
> largely because he reported losing much more money than he made.
>
> —[The New York
> Times](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2020/09/27/us/donald-trump-
> taxes.html), September 27, 2020

> Trump Organization found guilty of tax fraud in scheme hatched by top
> executives
>
> —[PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/donald-trumps-company-found-
> guilty-of-tax-fraud-in-scheme-hatched-by-top-executives), December 6, 2022

Frank J. Bisignano is the[ Chief Executive Officer of the Internal Revenue
Service](https://www.irs.gov/about-irs/ceo-frank-bisignano)when he is not
working as the[ Commissioner of the Social Security
Administration](https://www.ssa.gov/history/bisignano.html). Yes, he
simultaneously holds both positions. Bisignano told Congress that[ the current
IRS staffing level is
perfect](https://www.govexec.com/workforce/2026/03/after-
shedding-25000-employees-irs-chief-says-his-agency-now-has-perfect-staffing-
level/411890/). There is reason to be skeptical about Bisignano’s claim, and
not just because there is no dedicated full-time CEO of the IRS. The IRS
workforce was cut by[ 27 percent last
year](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/budget/2026/04/trumps-2027-budget-
request-doubles-down-on-agency-reorganizations-panned-by-congress/). There are
fewer people working at the IRS today than there were in[ the
mid-1980s](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/hiring-retention/2025/01/irs-
workforce-surpasses-100000-employees-but-faces-war-of-attrition-retaining-
staff/) while our tax system has become more complex and the population has
grown by 50 percent.

President Trump’s budget calls for a cut of[ $1.4 billion or 12.5
percent](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/budget/2026/04/trumps-2027-budget-
request-doubles-down-on-agency-reorganizations-panned-by-congress/) from the
IRS’ budget. This is after IRS funding was cut[ 9
percent](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/14/irs-budget-cut-2026.html) last year,
the[ fourth consecutive year of flat or reduced
funding](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/14/irs-budget-cut-2026.html).

This was not supposed to happen. Seeing that the IRS was[ grossly
understaffed](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/hiring-retention/2025/01/irs-
workforce-surpasses-100000-employees-but-faces-war-of-attrition-retaining-
staff/), was[ operating using technology from the 1960s](https://itep.org/irs-
funding-cuts-inflation-reduction-act-tax-avoidance/), and was using places
like a cafeteria and hallways as[ storage rooms for some of the 10.2 million
unprocessed paper tax
returns](https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/interactive/2022/irs-
pipeline-tax-return-delays/), the Biden administration succeeded in obtaining
funding for the IRS in the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 to address these
and other problems. But[Republicans outmaneuvered the Democrats in the
following years](https://itep.org/irs-funding-cuts-inflation-reduction-act-
tax-avoidance/), and now much of that funding has been clawed back. This
continues[ the tradition of Republican leaders attacking
IRS](https://itep.org/irs-funding-cuts-inflation-reduction-act-tax-
avoidance/), making it easier for the rich to avoid paying their taxes.

A major problem for our country’s finances is that there is about[ $700
billion per year](https://budgetlab.yale.edu/research/revenue-and-
distributional-effects-irs-funding) in tax evasion. This means that the
country has larger deficits and has more difficulty paying for all the things
the government does like health care, education, veterans’ benefits, and so
on. Most of this tax evasion occurs among the rich.[Nearly 30
percent](https://budgetlab.yale.edu/research/revenue-and-distributional-
effects-irs-funding) of unpaid tax dollars are due to tax evasion from the
richest 1 percent.[ Half of all unpaid tax
dollars](https://budgetlab.yale.edu/research/revenue-and-distributional-
effects-irs-funding) are due to the top 5 percent.

The Yale Budget Lab estimated that the increased IRS funding in the Inflation
Reduction Act would have brought in[ over $600 billion in revenue over 10
years](https://budgetlab.yale.edu/research/revenue-and-distributional-effects-
irs-funding). Now, because of the success of the[ anti-IRS movement by
Republicans in Congress](https://itep.org/irs-funding-cuts-inflation-
reduction-act-tax-avoidance/), much of that revenue is lost. The IRS division
that audits billionaires has been pushed to cut[ 38 percent of its
staff](https://www.visaverge.com/news/treasury-inspector-general-warns-irs-
struggles-as-white-house-seeks-inflation-reduction-act-funding/).

Billionaire tax cheats are breathing easier.
